**Ch 022 draft**

Candidate: *"He's sick they say, but is getting better?"*

In the source, this is Ishmael's statement: *"No, we hav'n't. He's sick they say, but is getting better, and will be all right again before long."* The stranger then laughs derisively at "All right again before long!" — which is the pivot the stranger mocks.

In the draft, the line is rendered as a question put by the stranger: *"He's sick they say, but is getting better?"* — and then "So they tell us" is Ishmael's reply. The stranger's laugh ("All right again before long!") then has no antecedent assertion to mock — the stranger is laughing at his own question. The logical structure is: stranger mocks Ishmael's confident assertion that Ahab will be "all right again before long." In the draft, that confident assertion by Ishmael is gone; instead the stranger asks a question and then laughs derisively at a reply of "So they tell us." The derisive laugh still attaches to something, so the pivot is not completely severed — but the specific phrase "All right again before long!" that the stranger quotes back and mocks has no source in the draft dialogue. A reader sees the stranger laughing at "All right again before long!" when no one said that.

This is a **broken pivot**: the stranger's derisive repetition of "All right again before long!" quotes words that, in the draft, were never spoken by Ishmael. The triggering statement was reassigned to the stranger as a question, so his mocking echo has no referent in the draft.

Candidate: *"and the prediction of the squaw Tistig"*

Tistig is not introduced anywhere in the draft (or in the surviving source for Ch 021–022 draft). In the source of Ch 022, this reference appears in the same list and the squaw Tistig is never introduced in Ch 22's source either — she is mentioned in Ch 019 source. This is not an authorized cut of a character, and "squaw Tistig" is never glossed or introduced in either draft chapter. However, she appears identically in both source and draft in the same list-of-anxieties passage, so this is carried over from source intact — not a compression artifact. A reader could be puzzled but it's equally puzzling in the source. Not a finding.
